hero.kicker: For export SMEs and the banks that fund them
hero.title: Stay ahead of cash flow. Make financing decisions with confidence.
hero.lede: CashBridge reads your bank feed, invoices and shipping documents, forecasts 13 weeks of cash, prices every way to cover the gap, and drafts a funding pack. Your Director approves it with a one-time code; your lender re-verifies every hash.
hero.fine: All companies, people, lenders and bank feeds in this demo are synthetic or mocked.
chart.title: 13-week cash forecast
chart.gap: First negative week, found by the forecast
chart.residual: Scenarios that never run short: one advance vs the recommended plan
flow.title: How a case runs
flow.lede: One loop, five steps. The software reads the documents and does the arithmetic; people make the two decisions that matter.
s1.d: Forecasts 13 weeks from open invoices, deposits and payroll, and names what causes the first negative week.
s2.d: Matches bank credits to invoices, checks each invoice against its purchase order and bill of lading, and blocks lookalike-domain payment emails.
s3.d: Prices factoring, a bridge loan and early-payment discounts as a true annual cost, then stress-tests the choice week by week.
s4.d: Reviews the pack the accountant prepared and releases it with a one-time code bound to that exact pack. The preparer cannot approve.
s5.d: Sees only what was released, recomputes every document hash and the audit chain, and records the credit decision.
portals.title: Two portals, one evidence trail
portals.lede: Each side signs in separately. Permissions are enforced by the server, so hiding a button grants nothing.

p.sme.c3: Test what-ifs: slower buyers, smaller deposits, FX moves
p.sme.c5: Check how safe a plan is across 2,000 scenarios before you commit
p.sme.c4: Review contracts, bids, budgets and green-investment evidence

p.bank.x2: No automated credit decision: a named person decides

trust.lede: Run make trust to reproduce these numbers. They come from the same code that serves this page.
trust.sec: Adversarial requests refused or detected: forged sessions, self-approval, replayed codes, double financing, tampered documents, prompt injection
trust.agent: Autopilot scenarios end correctly, including the ones where the right move is to stop or hand over to a person
trust.model: Brier score of the buyer payment model against the historical-rate baseline, walk-forward on 167 synthetic invoices: synthetic data, indicative only
cl.works.d: Forecast, matching, APR, coverage and stress engines; OTP-bound approval; hash-chained audit log and invoice registry; server-side roles for both portals.
cl.mock.d: Bank feeds, the lender connector and its price list, buyer KYC. The data set is synthetic.
cl.not.d: Cross-lender duplicate checks, production identity management, legal review of contracts, credit approval, green taxonomy certification.
foot: Built for the 2026 Shenzhen International FinTechathon, Topic E: SME Finance Copilot. Synthetic data only; not a bank, not financial advice.

cash.title: Cash forecast
cash.lede: Thirteen weeks from today, built from open invoices and confirmed orders weighted by each buyer's chance of paying on time, supplier deposits, fixed costs and payroll. Unconfirmed sales are not assumed.

core.lede: The planning engine (Intelligence Core): compares every allowed financing plan across simulated scenarios, picks the cheapest one that meets the goal, and updates its model only after a person approves. It cannot submit, pay or change a limit.

core.goal.keep_above_buffer: Keep every week above the cash buffer

core.packNote: Each factoring or loan is its own pack: the accountant drafts it and the Director approves it with a one-time code. The Core drafts nothing.
core.rankedSub: Allowed plans compared under the same simulated conditions.
core.memorySub: From case memory. SIMULATED quarters are replayed in a hidden test world, not real history.

oc.title: On-chain register and audit anchor

oc.note: {network}. Real EVM bytecode; the other consortium lenders are simulated accounts in this process. Nothing about the invoice (seller, buyer, number, amount) is written on chain. A testnet deploy script exists but was not run.
